inventedEvidence.evidence: 'If the thermometer shows a very different temperature, you've confirmed the thermostat is faulty' implies a thermometer reading was available; also the assistant never asked the customer to get one, and the customer had no reading.

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'That inconsistent light cycle is a classic sign of a mechanical thermostat that has lost its calibration or is failing internally'

unjustifiedPart.evidence: 'you will need to call an engineer to fit the new thermostat safely'

rationale: The assistant jumped to a confident thermostat diagnosis without temperature measurement. It ignored other plausible causes the customer's evidence pointed to (flattened door seal, inconsistent preheating, wobbly knob) and never suggested a cheap oven thermometer even though the customer said they had none. It did correctly route the mains work to an engineer, but the 'new thermostat' conclusion was unsupported, and the earlier request to inspect the elements was a poor, unanswerable check. The 'thermometer' reference also appeared out of nowhere in the third reply.
